title: Autonomic VPC egress prober and rolling upgrade orchestration module
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Private/VPC deployments sometimes experience silent egress failures after Terraform-driven network upgrades (route table changes, NAT replacement, IGW swap). We need a composable Terraform module and small orchestration layer to: 1) provision zone-aware subnets + NAT/IGW patterns; 2) create VPC endpoints and route table associations; 3) attach health probes that detect broken egress paths (per-subnet synthetic probes to external endpoints and to internal infra like package registries); and 4) provide rolling upgrade hooks that coordinate safe replacement of NATs/IGWs and route table swaps with minimal customer disruption.

Goal: Deliver a Terraform module (reusable) and a lightweight operator/orchestration runbook that together enable safe automated upgrades, automated reconciliation of endpoint policies, and an observational surface (metrics/alerts + console links) to surface failures quickly to SRE/SEs. The module should be idempotent, support a canary subset of subnets for smoke validation, and include a small plan for migration/rollback in case of regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module locatable under modules/vpc-egress-orchestrator with documented inputs/outputs
Module supports: zonal-subnet groups, optional NAT gateways per AZ, IGW fallback, route table templating, and VPC endpoint CRUD with policy attachments
Automated per-subnet synthetic probe (lambda/container) created by module that validates: outbound TCP/443 to trusted external endpoint, DNS resolution test, and NAT IP verification
A "canary" toggle to run probes only for a configurable subset of subnets
A rolling upgrade plan that replaces NAT/IGW one AZ at a time, waits for probe success, and supports abort/rollback
Terraform plan/apply produces clear change summary and fails fast on drifted route table associations
Dashboards and alerts created: per-subnet probe success rate, per-AZ egress latency, and upgrade-failure alert routed to SRE
End-to-end test: simulate NAT replacement in staging and show zero application-level 5xx increase and <5% p99 latency delta
Module documentation includes upgrade playbook, diagnostics steps, and links to GitHub PR and Console dashboards
tasks: Design terraform module API and inputs (CIDR patterns, az_count, nat_mode=single-per-az|shared, endpoints list)
Implement route table templating with explicit association blocks and lifecycle rules
Add provisioning of per-subnet synthetic prober (container run on Fargate or lambda) with IAM least-privilege
Implement canary toggle and tagging to scope probes to a subset of subnets
Create orchestration script (Go/python) to coordinate rolling replacements and validate probe results
Wire metrics to CloudWatch/Prometheus and build Grafana/Console dashboard panels
Create alerting playbooks and PagerDuty escalation mapping
Write e2e test harness for staging that runs a simulated NAT swap and verifies acceptance criteria
Prepare Terraform examples and upgrade playbook in docs/ with troubleshooting section
notes: Design tradeoffs: prefer NAT Gateway (managed) for most customers, but support NAT instance pattern for air-gapped or cost-sensitive installs
Probing endpoint should be stable and globally reachable (suggestion: public healthcheck endpoint maintained by infra team or provider-specific endpoint)
We must avoid introducing cross-AZ traffic charges during canary (keep probes in same AZ where possible)
Operator should honor maintenance windows via resource tags and optional 'pause-upgrades' flag
We will reuse existing RBAC/KMS patterns from private-deployments to avoid new security primitives
risks: Synthetic probes could themselves create noisy/expensive traffic if misconfigured
Incorrect route table lifecycle rules may orphan routes during upgrades if not carefully ordered
IAM scope for probe runner must be least privilege; otherwise it creates an attack surface
Edge case: provider rate limits for creating/deleting NAT resources in bulk during large upgrades
qa_steps: Deploy module into isolated staging VPC and enable canary probes for one subnet per AZ
Run terraform plan and verify no destructive changes expected when toggling canary flag
Trigger a scripted NAT replacement: coordinate orchestration script to replace NAT in AZ-a, validate probes, then proceed to next AZ
Simulate failure: force probe to fail after NAT swap and ensure orchestration performs abort and triggers rollback
Run load test against sample service to confirm no more than 5% p99 latency regression
Verify CloudWatch metrics and alert firing in the simulated failure scenario
deliverables: Orchestration CLI with dry-run and resume capabilities
Probe runner image and terraform provisioning for it
Grafana dashboard + alert rules + escalation mapping
Docs: design doc, upgrade playbook, troubleshooting guide, runbook for SRE

2026-03-02 - Design review: agreed on canary-by-tag approach instead of per-VPC boolean. Updated tasks and docs to reflect tag-based scoping.
